sec: Renal phosphate and the FGF23–Klotho axis

items.q: Proximal phosphate reclamation uses the ___ cotransporters and is powered by ___.
items.exp: The page names sodium–phosphate cotransporters IIa and IIc in the PCT and labels transport secondary active. (Book p888)

items.q: Which model best describes proximal tubular phosphate handling?
opts: Major NaPi-mediated uptake regulated by PTH and FGF23
Fixed 99% uptake unaffected by PTH or FGF23
Predominantly paracellular uptake regulated by calcitonin
Minor uptake with most recovery by collecting-duct NaPi
items.exp: The PCT is the major regulated site, but the printed 99% should not be taught as an invariant filtered-load reabsorption fraction. Hormones and intake change renal phosphate handling. (Book p888)

items.q: A child with glucosuria despite normal glucose, proximal bicarbonate wasting and severe rickets has which phosphate mechanism?
opts: Generalized proximal dysfunction causing phosphate wasting
Isolated distal acidification failure causing phosphate retention
Autonomous calcitriol excess causing phosphate retention
Absent PTH causing increased proximal phosphate uptake
items.exp: Fanconi syndrome involves generalized PCT dysfunction, phosphate depletion and severe mineralization defects. Isolated type II RTA need not imply the full Fanconi syndrome. (Book p888)

items.q: An early-CKD patient still has a normal serum phosphate despite declining filtration. Which compensation explains this?
opts: FGF23 suppression of proximal NaPi transport
FGF23 activation of proximal NaPi transport
Loss of every renal Klotho receptor
items.exp: FGF23 reduces NaPi transport, increases phosphaturia and can maintain normal serum phosphate early in CKD. (Book p888)

items.q: FGF23 inhibits renal ___, reducing calcitriol-mediated calcium absorption and contributing to secondary HPT.
items.exp: The diagram connects FGF23 inhibition of 1α-hydroxylase to lower calcium absorption and secondary hyperparathyroidism. (Book p888)

items.q: Assess: I High phosphate in advanced CKD proves FGF23 concentrations are low. II The source attributes reduced FGF23 effectiveness to impaired Klotho signaling.
items.exp: The source calls this 'FGF23 inactivated' due to Klotho resistance; this is impaired effectiveness, not evidence that circulating FGF23 concentrations are low. (Book p888)

items.q: Match the following vascular concepts — 1) CKD phosphate-associated calcification 2) Atherosclerotic calcification 3) Mineralizing vascular-cell phenotype … A) Medial B) Intimal C) Osteoblast-like
items.exp: The source contrasts medial calcification in CKD with intimal calcification in atherosclerosis and depicts osteogenic transformation of vascular cells. (Book p888)

items.q: An advanced-CKD diagram ends with 'unfit for renal transplant' after medial calcification. How should this endpoint be interpreted clinically?
opts: A simplified warning requiring individualized vascular assessment
An automatic permanent exclusion for every calcified vessel
Evidence that phosphate must be low before evaluation begins
Proof that atherosclerotic calcification is always medial
items.exp: Severe vascular calcification can complicate transplant suitability, but the diagram's categorical endpoint is not a universal eligibility rule. (Book p888)

items.q: Match the following net mineral effects — 1) PTH 2) Vitamin D 3) FGF23 … A) Raises Ca, lowers phosphate B) Promotes phosphate excretion C) Raises Ca and phosphate
items.exp: PTH raises calcium while promoting phosphaturia; vitamin D raises absorption of both; FGF23 promotes phosphate excretion. (Book p888)

items.q: Evaluate the feedback notes: I PTH promotes vitamin D activation, and vitamin D stimulates FGF23. II FGF23 normally inhibits PTH and active-vitamin-D production.
items.exp: The notes depict PTH → vitamin D → FGF23 stimulation, with FGF23 negative feedback on PTH and vitamin D; resistance can modify this in CKD. (Book p888)

items.q: The two bone-cell products named at the bottom of the page are ___ and ___.
items.exp: The source groups FGF23 and sclerostin under osteoblast secretion. More precisely, osteocytes are important sources, particularly for sclerostin. (Book p888)
